internship.title: Python Development Internship
internship.description: A role-specific Python Development Internship where students learn through realistic requirements, implementation, testing, review and delivery.
internship.learningModel: learn -> inspect -> implement -> test -> review -> iterate -> deliver
expectations: Complete every practical and dedicated task.
Verify work instead of assuming it works.
completionRequirements: Explain submitted work during final review.

modules.description: Understand project structure, virtual environments, dependencies, Git workflow and Python tooling.

lessons.description: Understand project structure, virtual environments, dependencies, Git workflow and Python tooling.
learningObjectives: Apply the concept to a realistic internship project.

notes.text: Understand project structure, virtual environments, dependencies, Git workflow and Python tooling.

This module follows a real engineering workflow. Students should inspect the existing project before changing it, understand the requirement, implement a focused solution, verify it, document important decisions and prepare it for review.

notes.alt: Python Development Internship — Python Internship Onboarding
notes.caption: Add a dedicated diagram or annotated screenshot showing Python Internship Onboarding in a real development workflow.

notes.text: First understand the problem, then the underlying professional Python application development concept, then apply it to the project. The student should be able to explain both what was done and why.

items: Read the requirement or issue.
Inspect existing code and data flow.
Break the work into small changes.
Implement the smallest correct solution.
Run tests/checks and inspect the result.
Test an edge or failure case.
Compare the result with acceptance criteria.
Document the implementation and limitations.

notes.code: Set up the repository and run its tests.

items: Changing unfamiliar code without tracing its current behavior.
Ignoring error, empty or boundary states.
Skipping verification after implementation.
Creating unnecessary abstractions.
Committing secrets or environment-specific credentials.
Keep changes focused and reviewable.
Use meaningful names and clear boundaries.
Test important behavior, not just the happy path.
Follow existing project conventions unless there is a reason to change them.
Document important assumptions and limitations.

I can trace the relevant project flow.
I can implement the basic requirement.
I can test an edge/failure case.
